s1.syndrome_frame: Subacute onset of pain and swelling around the scapula and ankle with systemic symptoms
salient_findings: Pain and swelling around the right scapula
Fever
Swelling and pain of the left ankle
Elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate and C-reactive protein level
Magnetic resonance imaging findings consistent with osteomyelitis
key_facts: 18-year-old man
20 days of pain and swelling around the right scapula
2 days of fever
Receiving anti-tubercular therapy for 6 months
Diagnosis of presumed pulmonary tuberculosis based on cough, chest radiograph findings, and elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate
Negative sputum studies
Swelling and pain of the left ankle with difficulty walking
Erythrocyte sedimentation rate of 73 mm/h
Positive C-reactive protein level of 96 mg/L
Magnetic resonance imaging findings consistent with osteomyelitis involving the scapula and the distal tibia

raw.rationale: The patient's history of receiving anti-tubercular therapy for presumed pulmonary tuberculosis and the development of osteomyelitis involving the scapula and the distal tibia, as shown by magnetic resonance imaging, support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Chronic osteomyelitis
rejected.why: Lack of specific evidence for a chronic infection other than tuberculosis

rejected.label: Bacterial osteomyelitis
rejected.why: The patient's context of anti-tubercular therapy and presumed pulmonary tuberculosis points more specifically to tuberculous osteomyelitis

rejected.label: Multidrug-resistant tuberculosis
rejected.why: While the patient is on anti-tubercular therapy, there is no direct evidence provided for multidrug resistance in this context

rejected.label: Chronic recurrent multifocal osteomyelitis
rejected.why: The patient's presentation and history do not align with the typical pattern of chronic recurrent multifocal osteomyelitis, which is more commonly associated with a different set of underlying conditions and does not typically involve tuberculosis
